{{Heart of Midlothian F.C. Departments}}
'''Heart of Midlothian Football Club''', commonly known as '''Hearts''', is a professional [[Association football|football]] club in [[Edinburgh]], Scotland. The team competes in the {{Scottish football updater|HeartofM}}, the top division of [[Scottish football league system|Scottish football]]. Hearts, the oldest football club in the Scottish capital,<ref>{{cite book |last= Bowie|first=Andrew-Henry |date=2011 |title=Two miles to Tynecastle |location=Clacton on Sea |publisher=Apex}}</ref> was formed in 1874, its name influenced by [[Walter Scott]]'s novel ''[[The Heart of Midlothian]]'' (1818).<ref name="1874-1884"/> The club crest is based on the [[Heart of Midlothian (Royal Mile)|''Heart of Midlothian'' mosaic]] on the city's [[Royal Mile]]; the team's colours are maroon and white.<ref name="1874-1884"/> Their local rivals are [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], with whom they contest the [[Edinburgh derby]]. The club has been majority supporter-owned through [[Foundation of Hearts]] since 2021.

Hearts have played home matches at [[Tynecastle Park]] since 1886.<ref name = "Inglis447">{{harvnb|Inglis|1996|p=447}}</ref> After the ground was converted into an all-seater stadium in 1994, it now has a capacity of {{SPFL-stadiums|hearts}}<ref name=capacity/> following the completion of a rebuilt main stand in 2017. They have training facilities at the [[Oriam]], Scotland's national performance centre for sport, where they also run their [[Heart of Midlothian F.C. Reserves and Academy|youth academy]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/performance/oriam/ |title=Oriam - The jewel in the crown of Scottish sport |work=Scottish FA |access-date=24 September 2018}}</ref>

Hearts have won the [[List of Scottish football champions|Scottish league championship]] four times, most recently in [[1959–60 Scottish Division One|1959–60]], when they also retained the [[1959 Scottish League Cup final|Scottish League Cup]] to complete a [[Double (association football)#League & League Cup Double|League and League Cup double]] – the only club outside of the [[Old Firm]] to achieve such a feat.

The club's most successful period was under former player turned manager [[Tommy Walker (footballer, born 1915)|Tommy Walker]] from the early 1950s to mid 1960s, during which they won two league titles and five major cups and finished inside the league's top four positions for 11 consecutive seasons. [[Jimmy Wardhaugh]], [[Willie Bauld]] and [[Alfie Conn Sr.]], known as the Terrible Trio, were forwards at the start of this period with wing half linchpins [[Dave Mackay]] and [[John Cumming (Scottish footballer)|John Cumming]]. Wardhaugh was part of another notable Hearts attacking trinity in the [[1957–58 Scottish Division One|1957–58]] league winning side: along with [[Jimmy Murray (footballer, born 1933)|Jimmy Murray]] and [[Alex Young (footballer, born 1937)|Alex Young]],<ref name=lh1956>{{cite web|url=http://www.londonhearts.com/scores/sea/1957-58.html|title=1957-58|website=Londonhearts.com|access-date=27 July 2018}}</ref> they set the record for the number of goals scored in a Scottish top-flight winning campaign (132) and also became the only side to finish a season in the Scottish top tier with a goal difference exceeding 100 (+103).

Hearts have won the [[Scottish Cup]] eight times, most recently in [[2012 Scottish Cup final|2012]] after a 5–1 victory over Hibernian.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/18044372|title=Hibernian 1 Hearts 5|date=19 May 2012|work=BBC Sport|access-date=22 May 2012}}</ref> They have since been runners up in [[2019 Scottish Cup final|2019]], [[2020 Scottish Cup final|2020]] and [[2022 Scottish Cup final|2022]]. All four of Hearts' [[Scottish League Cup]] triumphs came under Walker, most recently a 1–0 victory against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] in [[1962 Scottish League Cup final|1962]]. Their most recent League Cup Final appearance was in [[2013 Scottish League Cup final|2013]], where they lost 3–2 to [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].

In 1958, Heart of Midlothian became the third [[Football in Scotland|Scottish]] and fifth [[Football in the United Kingdom|British]] team to compete in [[UEFA#Competitions|European competition]]. The club reached the quarter-finals of the [[1988–89 UEFA Cup]], losing to [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] 2–1 on aggregate."}}
